data.one_liner: Dart client for Atlassian REST APIs (Jira, Confluence, Service Desk, Cloud Admin).
data.what_it_does: It wraps Atlassian’s OpenAPI definitions into typed Dart classes, handling authentication, request building, and response parsing. The client supports all major Atlassian services and can upload files via multipart requests.
use_when: You need to integrate with Jira, Confluence, or Service Desk from a Dart/Flutter app.
You prefer a fully typed API client generated from OpenAPI schemas.
You want to avoid writing boilerplate HTTP code for Atlassian endpoints.
avoid_when: You only need a few specific endpoints and want a lightweight solution.
You are already using another HTTP client like dio and prefer to keep a single HTTP layer.
strengths: Fully typed, generated from official OpenAPI specs; reduces manual coding.
Supports authentication via API token or OAuth, and multipart uploads for attachments.
weaknesses: Relies on http package; no advanced features like interceptors or retry logic.
Requires manual updates when Atlassian changes schemas; you must bump the package version.
No built‑in caching or offline support.
data.setup_notes: Add dependency, create ApiClient with basicAuthentication, instantiate JiraPlatformApi or ConfluenceApi, call methods. No build_runner needed.

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: Basic HTTP client used internally; simpler if you only need raw requests.
